decision: U3: should auto-captured text become a memory record, in which table, at what importance
metric: single-label class over decision/error/context/rule/none on the test split. macro_f1 = mean F1 over the classes present in gold or predictions. false_capture_rate = gold none predicted as anything else / gold none (a junk record). wrong_table_rate = stored in the wrong table / (gold not none and stored). miss_rate = gold not none predicted none / gold not none. Importance accuracy is over gold not-none test items, whatever the arm's class.
control: production at the hook's --min-confidence 0.8 (the only automatic caller); production@0.7 is the CLI default, for reference
selection: see the script docstring; every model setting was chosen on train only
sampling_note: half of each source's quota went to texts containing a production pattern, so the regex fires more often here than on all hook traffic; rates are for this set

settings.tau_grid_note: the first run's grid stopped at 0.95; no zero-shot setting met the train false-capture bar there, so the grid was extended toward 1 and the zero-shot arms re-selected on train from their saved scores (--reselect); each arm keeps its first_selection

regex_refinement_needs: Context and rule records: 10 context and 3 rule test texts missed; analyze() has no pattern for either (CaptureType::Context exists but is never emitted, and there is no rule type), so the regex can only ever store errors and decisions.

Errors: 17 of 22 error test texts missed (by source: {'agent_text': 8, 'commit_subject': 5, 'agent_brief': 2, 'bash_output': 1, 'bash_failure': 1}), 6 of them matched a pattern below the hook's 0.8 bar. In raw output only rustc error codes, panics and tracebacks reach 0.8 (0.6 base, +0.1 for the 'exit code' line every hook text starts with, +0.1 or +0.2 for the specific format); an agent's prose report of what broke carries none of the output-shaped patterns.

Decisions: 3 decision test texts missed: commit subjects and agent prose state the choice directly ("X stays", "scan exactly instead of ...") without the decision phrases. The one decision the hook bar stores is a false capture: a "decision:" list header inside a conditional plan, so the marker needs a guard for headers and conditionals (if, I'd).

Junk before the bar can move: at the CLI default 0.7, 13 gold-none test texts would also be stored as errors ({'zsh `=...` or glob error': 6, 'git refusing the command': 1, "regex parse error from the agent's own search": 4, 'a source line printed by a search': 1, 'usage error (missing argument)': 1}): command-line mistakes (guideline N4) and printed code (N2) that reach 0.7 only through the 'exit code' bonus. A guard list for these shapes, and for a non-zero exit that is the command's answer (grep found nothing, diff, test), has to come before any lower threshold.

Importance: compute_importance ignores the class and the failure's severity; on gold not-none test texts its bucket accuracy is 0.4737 with cut points fit on train, against the always-the-most-common-bucket baseline in importance_majority_baseline.
